Policy evaluated: Online game curfew (midnight to 6 AM), under-16s
Design: Difference-in-differences with regression discontinuity at age 16 and propensity score matching, on individual game-server logs
N: (individual gamer logs; heavy = top 20% by prior play)
Primary outcome: Total play time, minutes, and spending
Effect estimate: Light gamers (bottom 80%) −108.752 min (P < .01). Heavy gamers (top 20%) +0.173 min, ie, no effect. Within the treatment group, heavy gamers lost 154.9 and 41.1 min in the two curfew slots but gained 20.9, 69.8, 70.1, 74.3 and 37.6 min across the daytime and evening slots, a net increase. Spending did not change.

Policy evaluated: Online game curfew, second independent evaluation
Design: Multiple regression on repeated national cross-sections
Primary outcome: Internet hours, internet addiction, sleep duration
Effect estimate: Sleep duration +1.5 min. Internet addiction probability −0.7 percentage points. Probability of being a high-ranked internet user +1.6 percentage points. Effects differed by sex.
